method: Double elimination in a power-of-two draw. Every entrant starts in the winners bracket; one defeat drops them into the losers bracket and a second ends their run, so n teams play 2n-2 matches, or 2n-1 when a reset final is played. The winners bracket is a single-elimination tree: round k plays n/2^k matches and its losers drop into the matching major stage of the losers bracket. The losers bracket alternates minor and major rounds. An odd losers round pairs survivors of the previous losers round with each other, and the first one pairs the n/2 losers of winners round 1; an even losers round pairs the winners of the previous losers round with the losers of the same-numbered winners round, so each pair of losers rounds halves the bracket. That yields 2p-2 losers rounds and n-2 matches for p = log2(n) levels, which with the winners bracket's n-1 gives the published 2n-2 game count, one or two fewer than twice the teams. The page refuses any field other than 4, 8, 16 or 32 teams: a bye in a double-elimination draw leaves a losers-bracket slot that has to be settled by a walkover or a reseed, and the model does not invent one. Rounds are reported as blocks in playing order - winners round 1, losers round 1, then for each further winners round its major losers round followed by the next minor one, then the final - because a block cannot start before the matches that feed it finish, so a block costs ceil(matches / stations) match lengths. The plan reports that block time, the perfect-packing floor of ceil(total / stations) blocks, the total station time, and the longest route to the title: 2p matches for a first-round loser who wins the whole draw, one more with a reset. A single final eliminates the losers-bracket champion with one defeat, which is why the game count can land one short; a reset final replays it only when the losers-bracket side wins the first. Inputs are limited to 5-180 minute matches and 1-16 stations, and text, fractional and out-of-range values are refused with the field named. Seeding order, court assignment, walkovers, divisions and clock times are not modelled, and the page stores nothing and makes no requests.
